children: Oil prices have climbed back above $100 a barrel as escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and attacks on energy infrastructure in the Middle East raise concerns about further disruptions to global crude supplies.
The renewed strength in oil prices is also putting oil and gas stocks in focus, particularly companies with strong quantitative fundamentals.

Brent crude recently moved above $100 a barrel after a fresh wave of strikes involving the U.S. and Iran, marking its highest level since July. Oil had previously crossed the $100 threshold in late July as the conflict intensified, with Houthi attacks on Saudi oil tankers and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz adding to supply concerns.
Brent subsequently retreated as hopes of de-escalation emerged, highlighting the sensitivity of crude prices to developments in the region.

The latest escalation has once again raised concerns about the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global energy supplies. The conflict has also been compounded by attacks from Iran-backed Houthi forces on Saudi energy infrastructure, increasing the risk of further disruptions across key oil-producing and transportation hubs.
